title: Interactive benchmark page requirements + analytics event spec
creator: Henry Cho
description:
Context
We are shipping a public-facing interactive benchmark experience (tables + filters) as part of the benchmark report launch. This ticket defines the functional requirements and the analytics events (interaction + conversion) needed for GTM KPI reporting and post-launch iteration.

Primary owners/partners
- PM: Henry Cho
- Web Eng: Felix Schneider (interactive tables/filters), Alicia Perez (UX)
- Marketing ops/attribution: Tyler Benson
- Growth funnel: Ben Carter
- PMM: Soojin Lee
- Telemetry: Logan Wright
- Legal (claims/disclaimers): Michael Grant, Sofia Mendes

Source docs
- Confluence PRD (canonical): sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/interactive-benchmark-page-requirements.json
- Web experience spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/benchmark-report-web-experience-spec.json

Goals
1) Let developers answer: “Which model + region is best for my workload?” quickly and credibly.
2) Provide transparent definitions for latency/$ + supporting metrics, with clear caveats.
3) Instrument the page so we can quantify what drives signups/demos and where users drop off.

Non-goals
- We are not building a generalized BI product or long-term benchmarking program UI in v1.
- No logged-in experience required for v1 (public page). Optional: later reuse inside Console.

Functional requirements (v1)
A. Data + table behavior
- Data source is a versioned public benchmark artifact (JSON/CSV) delivered via the results service + CDN caching.
- Default view should load with a sensible baseline filter (e.g., popular models, region = user’s inferred geography if available; otherwise “All regions”).
- Table supports sorting and stable tie-breaking. Sorting defaults:
  - Primary: “latency/$ (higher is better)” OR “$ per 1M tokens (lower is better)”. Final default TBD with PMM + Legal.
  - Secondary: p95 latency (lower is better).
- Provide a “Last updated” timestamp and “Dataset version” identifier on page.

B. Filters
Required filters:
- Model (multi-select)
- Region (multi-select)
- Context length / prompt size bucket (e.g., 1k/4k/8k/16k; reflect how the benchmark buckets are defined)
- Workload type (or scenario): production mix (prefill+decode), prefill-heavy, decode-heavy (must match methodology naming)
- Concurrency level (if we can present without overwhelming; otherwise in v1 via “Scenario” presets)

Nice-to-have (ok to defer if it adds complexity/latency):
- Hardware profile toggle (if results are mixed across fleets; otherwise keep as metadata)
- “Hosted vs Dedicated” toggle (only if datasets are comparable and legally approved)

C. Metric toggles (top-level)
Required metric views:
- Latency/$ (definition displayed in tooltip with a “How we measured” link)
- p50 latency
- p95 latency
- Throughput (tokens/sec) OR equivalent throughput proxy (must align with Applied ML methodology)
- Cost: $ per 1M tokens

Rules/notes:
- Make it explicit when a metric is derived/normalized.
- If any metric is not available for a model/region/scenario, show “—” with a tooltip explaining why (e.g., “insufficient stable runs” / “excluded due to variance gate”).

D. Export + sharing
- Export current table view to CSV (minimum). JSON export optional if already supported by the artifact schema.
- “Copy link” that encodes current filters in query params.
- Exports must include dataset version + timestamp in file name.

E. Disclaimers + methodology
- Prominent but not disruptive disclaimer block near top and/or directly above table.
- “How we measured” should deep-link to a public methodology page/section.
- Tooltips for:
  - What is latency/$
  - What is included/excluded
  - Variance/stability notes (e.g., rerun thresholds)
- Legal requirement: avoid absolute claims without qualifying conditions; do not imply competitor data parity unless sourced and approved.

F. Accessibility + performance
- AA accessibility target; table must be keyboard navigable; tooltips must be accessible.
- Page performance:
  - Initial contentful paint should not be blocked by full dataset fetch.
  - Ensure dataset payload size is bounded; paginate/virtualize if needed.
  - Caching strategy must avoid cache-miss storms during launch traffic.

Analytics requirements (events + properties)
We need both interaction analytics (product insight) and conversion analytics (GTM funnel). Events must map to the benchmark launch campaign tagging conventions.

Event naming conventions
- Prefix: benchmark_
- Use snake_case
- Include dataset_version in all relevant events

Required events (v1)
1) benchmark_page_view
- When: page loads
- Properties: dataset_version, page_path, referrer, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, geo_region_inferred (if available), device_type

2) benchmark_filter_change
- When: any filter is changed (model/region/context/scenario)
- Properties: dataset_version, filter_name, filter_value (stringified), previous_value (stringified), results_count

3) benchmark_sort_change
- When: sort column or direction changes
- Properties: dataset_version, sort_key, sort_direction, results_count

4) benchmark_metric_toggle
- When: user switches metric view
- Properties: dataset_version, metric_name

5) benchmark_row_expand (only if we add expandable details)
- When: user expands a row for details
- Properties: dataset_version, model, region, scenario

6) benchmark_export_click
- When: export triggered
- Properties: dataset_version, export_format (csv/json), current_filters (stringified), results_count

7) benchmark_copy_link_click
- When: copy/share link clicked
- Properties: dataset_version, current_filters (stringified)

8) benchmark_methodology_click
- When: click to methodology/how-we-measured
- Properties: dataset_version, link_location (header/disclaimer/tooltip)

9) benchmark_cta_click
- When: any primary CTA clicked
- Required CTAs: “Start for free” (Hosted trial), “Talk to sales” (Dedicated/Private), “Request a sizing consult” (Dedicated)
- Properties: dataset_version, cta_type, cta_location (hero/table/footer), current_filters (stringified)

10) benchmark_signup_complete / benchmark_demo_request_submit (as applicable)
- When: downstream conversion event fires (owned by Growth/Ops)
- Properties: utm_campaign, campaign_tag (HubSpot), dataset_version (if available via carry-through), lead_type (plg/enterprise)

Instrumentation notes
- Ensure events are fired once per action; debounce filter changes (especially multi-select) to avoid noisy streams.
- For privacy: do not capture raw prompts, customer identifiers, or any unique token/trace IDs.
- Include a stable anonymous_id for session-level analysis (standard web analytics).

Acceptance criteria
- All required filters/metric toggles function correctly and are reflected in URL query params.
- Export produces accurate rows matching on-screen view and includes dataset_version.
- Disclaimers/tooltips present and match approved copy (PMM + Legal).
- Analytics events fire with required properties and pass QA in staging.
- Page remains responsive for large datasets (virtualization or pagination in place).

Open questions (to resolve before implementation lock)
1) Default metric: do we default to latency/$ or $/1M tokens? (PMM preference is latency/$; Legal wants clarity that it’s derived.)
2) Scenario representation: do we show concurrency as a filter or provide “scenario presets” to keep UI simpler?
3) Competitor baselines: will any competitor rows appear in the interactive table? If yes, we need separate disclaimer + source-of-truth gating.
4) Region naming: confirm canonical public region labels (e.g., eu-west vs “Frankfurt”) and which are publishable.

Rollout plan
- v1 behind a soft-launch flag on staging for internal review.
- Enable for public launch once Legal approves disclaimer language and data artifact version is locked.

Related work
- Results service + caching: ENG-18566
- Artifact export pipeline + redaction: ENG-18477
- Analytics instrumentation in product/web: PR-27905 (tracking) + Growth/Ops downstream events

Risks
- Launch traffic may spike; caching misconfig could degrade page latency (coordinate with SRE runbook).
- Over-instrumentation could slow the page; keep payloads lean and debounce events.
- Claim language in tooltips/disclaimers must match legal-approved text exactly.
comments: 2025-05-30 (Soojin Lee): Please keep the UI opinionated. Too many knobs will undercut the narrative. Suggest scenario presets (Production mix / Prefill-heavy / Decode-heavy) and hide concurrency unless user expands “Advanced”.

2025-06-01 (Tyler Benson): For attribution we need utms + a benchmark campaign tag carried through to HubSpot. Please ensure CTA links preserve query params; we’ve had issues with utm drop on redirects.

2025-06-03 (Felix Schneider): From a perf perspective: don’t load all columns by default; we can lazy-render or virtualize the table. Export will require full dataset fetch unless we export from server based on filters.

2025-06-04 (Logan Wright): Event schema looks good. Please specify whether filter_value should be a single string or list; recommendation: JSON-stringify arrays into a single property to avoid analytics pipeline issues.

2025-06-06 (Michael Grant): Disclaimer placement is critical—must be visible without scrolling on desktop. Also avoid “best”/“fastest” language without qualifying context (scenario + dataset version).

2025-06-10 (Henry Cho): Decision: keep concurrency out of v1 UI (baked into scenarios) to reduce confusion; we’ll still include concurrency metadata in the methodology page. Updated requirements accordingly.
2025-06-18 (Alicia Perez): Added requirement: keyboard navigation for filter chips and a11y-friendly tooltips. Also recommend showing “results_count” next to the table header for user trust.
2025-06-21 (Henry Cho): Marking Done: requirements reviewed with PMM/Growth/Telemetry; Legal notes incorporated. Implementation tracking continues in ENG tickets + DES-961.
